title: The Ligand Only Introduces Two Kinases

scenes.tts: Scientists purified a protein that, with E G F, made normal cells grow like tumour cells. They named it transforming growth factor beta. Then the same protein was caught holding other cells back. What does T G F beta do to a cell once it lands? Follow its message from the membrane to a gene.
scenes.visual: Ligand chip above a membrane; two tags (grows like a tumour cell, holds cells back) flank it then clear; a dashed chain of question-mark boxes runs from the membrane to a gene on DNA.
scenes.caption: Scientists purified a protein that, with EGF, made normal cells grow like tumour cells. They named it transforming growth factor beta. Then the same protein was caught holding other cells back. What does TGF-β do to a cell once it lands? Follow its message from the membrane to a gene.
scenes.narration: Scientists purified a protein that, with EGF, made normal cells grow like tumour cells. They named it transforming growth factor beta. Then the same protein was caught holding other cells back. What does TGF-β do to a cell once it lands? Follow its message from the membrane to a gene.

scenes.tts: The receptors for T G F beta are kinases of two types. The type two kinase is active before any ligand arrives. T G F beta is a dimer, two chains joined together. It binds two type two receptors. Then the ligand and type two together recruit two type one receptors. Four receptor chains now surround one ligand.
scenes.visual: Four receptor bars cross the membrane. Type II kinases glow green, type I are grey. The dimer lands on the two type II bars, then the two type I bars slide in beside them.
scenes.caption: The receptors for TGF-β are kinases of two types. The type II kinase is active before any ligand arrives. TGF-β is a dimer, two chains joined together. It binds two type II receptors. Then the ligand and type II together recruit two type I receptors. Four receptor chains now surround one ligand.
scenes.narration: The receptors for TGF-β are kinases of two types. The type II kinase is active before any ligand arrives. TGF-β is a dimer, two chains joined together. It binds two type II receptors. Then the ligand and type II together recruit two type I receptors. Four receptor chains now surround one ligand.

scenes.tts: Type two adds phosphate to a stretch of type one just inside the membrane, called the G S domain. At rest, the G S domain holds the type one kinase in an inactive shape. Phosphate ends that arrangement. The kinase turns on, and the stretch becomes a docking site for a Smad. Think of type two as a lit match, and type one as a fuse. The ligand only holds the match to the fuse.
scenes.visual: One type II and one type I kinase close up. A phosphate crosses from type II to the GS stretch of type I, which turns the type I kinase green and makes the GS stretch a docking slot.
scenes.caption: Type II adds phosphate to a stretch of type I just inside the membrane, called the GS domain. At rest, the GS domain holds the type I kinase in an inactive shape. Phosphate ends that arrangement. The kinase turns on, and the stretch becomes a docking site for a Smad. Think of type II as a lit match, and type I as a fuse. The ligand only holds the match to the fuse.

scenes.tts: The active type one kinase phosphorylates a Smad. A Smad is itself a transcription factor, a protein that binds D N A. T G F beta receptors phosphorylate Smad two and Smad three, on two serines at the end of the tail. A phosphorylated tail fits a pocket on a neighbouring Smad. So the Smads leave the receptor, and typically two of them join one Smad four.
scenes.visual: Two type I kinases each hold a Smad at the docking slot; two phosphates land on each Smad tail; the Smads detach, meet in the middle, and a single Smad4 joins them in a trio.
scenes.caption: The active type I kinase phosphorylates a Smad. A Smad is itself a transcription factor, a protein that binds DNA. TGF-β receptors phosphorylate Smad2 and Smad3, on two serines at the end of the tail. A phosphorylated tail fits a pocket on a neighbouring Smad. So the Smads leave the receptor, and typically two of them join one Smad4.
scenes.narration: The active type I kinase phosphorylates a Smad. A Smad is itself a transcription factor, a protein that binds DNA. So the Smads leave the receptor, and typically two of them join one Smad4.

scenes.tts: The complex collects in the nucleus and binds D N A. But it reads a sequence just a few base pairs long, and holds it weakly. That sequence turns up millions of times in a human genome, so a Smad complex alone cannot pick a gene. It binds firmly mostly next to partner proteins, and each cell type makes its own partners. In many epithelial cells, the partners turn on P fifteen and P twenty one, and the cell stops dividing. In a fibroblast, the same pathway turns on collagen genes.
scenes.visual: The Smad trio moves onto a stretch of DNA marked with many identical short sites and holds weakly. Partner chips arrive and it locks on. Epithelial case: p15 and p21 turn green. Everything resets; fibroblast case with different partners: collagen genes turn green.

scenes.tts: The ligand brings two kinases together. Type two phosphorylates type one, and type one phosphorylates a Smad. The steps run one way. In each cell, the partners decide what the message of the Smad means. Keep this rule: the ligand only introduces two kinases.
scenes.visual: A row: type II, type I, Smad, gene. The ligand sits above the first two. A phosphate hops along right-pointing arrows; partners are tagged under the Smad-to-gene step.
